title: GRPO Response Log Probabilities and KL
prompt:
Implement four PyTorch helpers for a language-model policy loss. Each prompt has a group of sampled responses and one reward per response.

### Contract

- `group_relative_advantages(rewards, group_size, eps=1e-6)`: return detached `[N]` rewards normalized within each consecutive group by its mean and population standard deviation plus `eps`. Constant and singleton groups return zeros.
- `gather_response_logprobs(logits, sequences, response_mask)`: return `[N, T-1]` next-token log probabilities. Output column `j` scores sequence token `j+1` using logits at `j`; it is zero when that token is masked out. There is no entry for sequence position zero.
- `masked_kl(policy_logits, reference_logits, response_mask)`: return scalar `KL(reference || policy)`, averaged over selected positions. Inputs are already aligned; the reference is fixed.
- `grpo_loss(...)`: return the negative advantage-weighted sum of response-token log probabilities, averaged over all `N` responses, plus `beta` times KL averaged over selected predictable tokens. Both terms score the same tokens; empty responses still count in `N`.

### Inputs and behavior

Logits are `[N, T, V]`, token IDs and boolean masks are `[N, T]`, and rewards are `[N]`. The KL helper accepts aligned `[N, S, V]` logits and an `[N, S]` mask.

Only policy logits receive gradients. Empty selections produce differentiable zeros with zero policy gradients. Preserve inputs and floating-point dtype/device.

Assume valid, finite CPU float32/float64 inputs with compatible dtypes and representable statistics: `N >= 1`, `T >= 2`, `V >= 1`, positive `group_size` dividing `N`, `eps > 0`, and `beta >= 0`. Input validation is not assessed.

This component objective uses token-summed log likelihood and exact KL, without importance ratios or clipping. For the full training loop, see [Debug a GRPO Training Loop](#/problems/grpo-training-loop-debugging?category=ML+Coding).
